contexts: regional orthopaedic centre, about 900 primary knee replacements a year
six weeks of group and home exercise after discharge
rural patients with poor mobile coverage
reading: The supplier's case rests on step counts, which feedback raises (claim c1), while the outcome that matters to patients and to the committee is function, where the retrieved review found no clear gain (claim c2). Walking volume may be a marker of recovery rather than its cause. Device wear falls over 12 weeks (claim c3) and stopping is more common among the oldest patients, people without smartphones and people living alone (claim c4), a large share of this centre's patients. Physiotherapist review time is small per patient but adds up across a caseload (claim c5).
